observations: Two shaft-like metal parts with ribbed CV boots on each end, consistent with vehicle drive/axle shafts, leaning against a wall.
A black metal assembly with a long splined rod and mounting bracket, consistent with a steering rack, mounted above the shafts.
A thin finned metal exchanger unit on the right, with an aluminum/thin-tube design; closer in appearance to an A/C condenser than a thick-tanked radiator, but tank ends are not visible.
A rounded metal cylindrical unit with a brass/copper-colored ring sitting on the ground, consistent in shape with a starter motor, but no markings or part number are legible.
A separate metal bracket resembling a brake caliper is visible at the bottom of the frame, not mentioned in the seller's list.
Surfaces show rust, dirt, and aged rubber boots; no vehicle badge, VIN plate, or part-number sticker is legible anywhere in the photo.
All items appear to be sitting outdoors against a rough plastered wall, consistent with scrap-yard style storage, not a showroom or tested bench.
